plan: In a second-price auction, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy. Since I pay the second-highest bid if I win (not my own bid), bidding exactly my value ensures I win whenever profitable (value > others' bids) and never overpay. Bidding higher risks negative profit if I win but pay more than value; bidding lower risks losing profitable opportunities. With value $47, I'll bid exactly $47 to maximize expected profit.

This is a second-price auction with independent private values. In such auctions, the dominant strategy is to bid exactly your true value, regardless of what others do. Bidding your value ensures: if you win, you pay the second-highest bid (which is less than your value, guaranteeing non-negative profit), and if you lose, it's because someone else valued it more than you did. There's no benefit to shading up or down from true value in a second-price auction. My value is $33, so I'll bid $33.

This is a second-price sealed-bid auction (highest bidder wins, pays second-highest bid). In such auctions, the dominant strategy is to bid exactly my true value, regardless of what others bid. This is because if I win, I pay the second-highest bid (not my own bid), so bidding my true value ensures I never overpay and always capture positive profit when I have the highest valuation. Bidding above value risks negative profit; bidding below value risks losing profitable opportunities. With no prior round history to suggest otherwise, I'll bid my true value of $36.
